vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.1.2

The skill bundle provides a legitimate workflow for automating the packaging and publishing of Chrome extensions to the Chrome Web Store. It includes scripts for generating marketing assets using headless Chrome, scanning local repositories for sensitive leaks (e.g., tokens or absolute paths in `scan_publish_surface.py`), and driving the developer dashboard via OpenClaw browser automation (`publish_extension.py`). The code is well-structured, lacks obfuscation, and its behavior is strictly aligned with the stated purpose of streamlining extension releases.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts broadly match a Chrome-extension packaging/publishing workflow, but the code is tightly tailored to a specific project (LocalLens / zack-dev-cm), scans arbitrary filesystem trees, and will drive the user's browser profile — these mismatches and privileged actions warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to build/package/scan/publish Chrome extensions using OpenClaw, GitHub, and ClawHub. The required binaries (python3, git, gh, clawhub, openclaw, sips) and the included scripts are consistent with that purpose. However, many scripts are hard-coded or opinionated for a specific project (notably references to 'LocalLens' and the GitHub owner 'zack-dev-cm'), which reduces general applicability and is inconsistent with a generic publisher skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to run scripts that will scan the provided search-root for extension manifests, read many files, render marketing HTML into screenshots, build ZIPs, run leak scans, and drive browser automation for publishing. Reading repository files and generating artifacts is expected, but the workflow will scan arbitrary filesystem trees (the user-supplied --search-root) and will use a browser profile for automation (potentially accessing logged-in sessions). That behavior is useful for publishing but carries privacy/credential risk and should be constrained by the user when running.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are included; the package is delivered as code files and uses local binaries. This is a low-risk install mechanism (scripts executed locally).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, which matches the code. However, it expects existing local tooling and browser profiles (openclaw/browser, gh, clawhub, sips). The skill will operate against the user's browser profile and copy artifacts into /tmp and the repo's dist directory — meaning it can leverage any active sessions (Chrome/Chrome Web Store) and local files without explicitly requesting credentials. Also, the manifest generation hardcodes URLs and text for a specific GitHub owner and extension name, which is not justified for a generic publisher.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal invocation settings. The code writes outputs to the repo (dist/, docs/) and uses /tmp for uploads and ephemeral profile dirs; it does not request persistent or system-wide privileges or attempt to alter other skills' config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill mostly does what it says, but exercise caution before running: 1) It is heavily tailored to a specific project (strings referencing 'LocalLens' and a GitHub owner 'zack-dev-cm') — if you plan to use it for a different extension, inspect and edit the manifest-generation and copy templates. 2) The inventory step scans a user-specified filesystem root and will read many files; pass a narrow, intentional --search-root (not your home directory) to avoid exposing unrelated repositories. 3) The publish flow drives your browser profile via OpenClaw and stages files under /tmp — that means it can use any active Chrome login/session for the Chrome Web Store. Use a dedicated browser profile without sensitive logins when publishing, or run the publish step only after reviewing publish_extension.py (the file was truncated in the package preview). 4) Run the tool in a sandbox or test workspace first, and review/modify hard-coded URLs, names, and policy text before using it for real releases.
